subarticles.title: Text Field — every setting
subarticles.summary: The free-text input field — what kind of value it accepts and how typed answers look. This guide documents every setting of the Text Field block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

subarticles.title: Text Field section
subarticles.summary: The Text Field section turns a screen into a question that collects a free-text answer such as a name, email, or goal. Set the placeholder hint, validation, and styling here; the answer is saved in a variable you can later use to branch the flow or personalize copy. Use it whenever the visitor should type an answer rather than pick from options — that captured input is what makes the screen gather usable data.

subarticles.title: Where it appears
subarticles.summary: Covered screen types: TextInput.

subarticles.title: Focus field when screen loads
subarticles.summary: When enabled, the field automatically receives focus and opens the keyboard when the screen appears. Default is true. Useful for primary input fields.

subarticles.title: Fill behind the input
subarticles.summary: Sets the fill color inside the input box. Most funnels leave it clear so the screen background shows through, or use a subtle light fill to make the tappable field stand out. Just make sure it contrasts with the typed-text color so answers stay easy to read and people don't abandon the question.

subarticles.title: Color of the field outline
subarticles.summary: Sets the color of the field's outline, which only appears when the Border Style is an underline or a full box. Use a tone from your theme — an accent or a soft neutral — so the field's edges read clearly as something to tap and type into. A visible outline helps people recognize and fill in the field.

subarticles.title: Space around the field
subarticles.summary: Sets the gap OUTSIDE the field, separating it from the title above and anything below, on the top, right, bottom, and left. Use it to give the field room to breathe within the screen. This is the space around the field — distinct from Internal Padding, which is the space inside it.

subarticles.title: Pick the field outline style
subarticles.summary: Chooses how the field is outlined: a bottom underline under the text, a bottom underline with room for an icon, or a full box around the whole field. A full box reads most clearly as a place to type, while underline styles feel lighter. Your pick here also decides whether the Border Color and Border Width settings actually show.

subarticles.title: Thickness of the outline
subarticles.summary: Controls how thick the field's outline is, from 0 to 50 pixels (default 1). Keep it at 1-2 pixels for a clean, modern look and only go thicker for a deliberately bold style. A visible but restrained outline helps people spot the field at a glance and answer faster.

subarticles.title: Fill behind the error text
subarticles.summary: Sets a fill color behind the validation error message that appears when an answer is rejected. Usually leave it transparent so only the red text shows; add a subtle tint only if you want the error to read like a banner. Whatever you choose, keep enough contrast with the error text so the message stays readable and users can quickly fix and continue.

subarticles.title: Font of the error text
subarticles.summary: Sets the typeface for the validation error message shown when an answer is rejected. Leave it on your theme/system font unless you have a specific brand font, and match it to the field's font so the error looks like part of the same form. A consistent error style keeps the screen feeling polished and helps users trust and fix the field fast.

subarticles.title: Size of the error text
subarticles.summary: Sets the point size of the validation error message. Keep it a touch smaller than the field text (about 12-13pt) so it reads as a secondary note, but not so small it's hard to read on a phone. A legible error helps users spot and fix a rejected answer instead of abandoning the screen.

subarticles.title: Boldness of the error text
subarticles.summary: Sets how heavy the error message looks (for example 400 regular or 600 semibold). Regular (400) works in most cases; step up to 600 if you want the error to stand out more. Paired with the red color, a bit more weight helps users notice and correct a rejected answer so they keep moving through the funnel.

subarticles.title: Set validation error message
subarticles.summary: Message displayed when user input fails validation (does not match Validation Regex or Field Type). Shown to guide correction. Can be localized per locale.

subarticles.title: Where the error text sits
subarticles.summary: Aligns the validation error message to the left, center, or right. Match it to the field's own text alignment (left is typical) so the message sits naturally under the input. Keeping them aligned makes it obvious which field was rejected, so users fix it quickly and don't stall.

subarticles.title: Color of the error message
subarticles.summary: Sets the color of the error text shown when an answer fails validation (default red, #FF3B30). Keep it red or another high-contrast warning color so people instantly see that their input was rejected and needs fixing. A clear error keeps them from giving up before they can continue.

subarticles.title: What the field accepts
subarticles.summary: Tells the field what kind of value to accept — plain text, a whole number, a decimal, a date, or an email — and automatically applies basic checks plus the right phone keyboard. Use Email for email capture and plain text for open answers. Picking the correct type blocks bad data, keeping any branching, analytics, or CRM that reads this answer reliable.

subarticles.title: Font for the field
subarticles.summary: Picks the font used for both the placeholder hint and what the visitor types. Leave it on the system font unless you have a brand font, and match whatever the rest of your funnel uses. Consistent type keeps the page feeling polished and trustworthy, which matters when you're paying for the traffic.

subarticles.title: Size of the field text
subarticles.summary: Sets how large the text in the field appears, from 0 to 50 points (default 15). Keep it around 15-17 points so answers are comfortable to read on a phone. Text that's too small is hard to read on mobile, where most ad traffic lands, and can quietly drag down completion.

subarticles.title: Weight of the field text
subarticles.summary: Sets how heavy the field text looks, from light (300) to bold (700), with regular (400) as the default. Regular is right for almost every input field. Keeping it regular makes the text read like an editable answer rather than a heading, so the field stays obvious and easy to use.

subarticles.title: Rounding the icon corners
subarticles.summary: Rounds the corners of the icon image (0-50px, default 0 for square). Leave it at 0 for normal line or glyph icons; raise it only for a photo or avatar-style icon you want to soften or make circular. It has little visible effect on transparent line icons, so most fields can skip it.

subarticles.title: Gap between icon and text
subarticles.summary: Sets the horizontal space between the field's icon and the text the visitor types (default 8 pixels). The default works for most fields — nudge it up a little if the icon and text feel cramped, or down for a tighter look. The goal is an icon and placeholder that sit comfortably balanced.

subarticles.title: Height of the field icon
subarticles.summary: Sets how tall the icon beside the input is (0-500px). Keep it around 20-24px so it lines up with the text, and usually match it to the icon width so the glyph stays square and undistorted. A right-sized icon reads as a helpful cue rather than visual clutter.

subarticles.title: How the icon fills its space
subarticles.summary: Controls how the icon sits inside its box: Fit keeps the whole image visible and may leave a little padding, Fill keeps proportions but crops the edges, and Stretch fills the box and can distort the image. Use Fit for logos and glyphs — it's the safe default — unless you specifically want a cropped or stretched look.

subarticles.title: Width of the field icon
subarticles.summary: Sets how wide the icon beside the input is (0-500px). Keep it small, around 20-24px, so it fits neatly next to the text, and usually match it to the icon height for a clean square glyph. Oversized icons crowd the field and make the input look heavier than it needs to.

subarticles.title: Optional icon in the field
subarticles.summary: Adds a small image — like a mail or person glyph — to the left of the input to hint at what the field is for. It's optional, and you can upload a different image for each language. It only appears with a Border Style that leaves room for an icon, and its size and rounding come from the icon's image style settings.

subarticles.title: Override mobile keyboard input type
subarticles.summary: Forces a specific keyboard on mobile devices (Email, Numeric, Decimal, Phone, URL, etc.). Leave as Auto (from field type) to let the system derive keyboard type from Field Type setting.

subarticles.title: Line spacing in the field
subarticles.summary: Sets the vertical gap between lines of typed text (0-50pt, default 18). It only shows when an answer wraps onto multiple lines, so for normal single-line questions leave it at the default. Adjust it only if you've allowed long, multi-line responses and they feel too cramped or too loose.

subarticles.title: Space inside the field
subarticles.summary: Sets the breathing room between the text or icon and the field's edges, on the top, right, bottom, and left. Generous spacing makes the field a bigger, easier tap target and keeps text from crowding the outline. If the field feels cramped on a phone, increase the top and bottom spacing.

subarticles.title: Color of the hint text
subarticles.summary: Sets the color of the faint hint shown while the field is empty, separate from the color of what the visitor types (default is a light gray, #999999). Keep it dimmer than the typed-text color so people can tell the hint from a real answer, but not so faint it disappears against your background.

subarticles.title: Set placeholder hint text
subarticles.summary: Hint text displayed in the field when empty, guiding users on what to enter. Can be localized per locale. Styling controlled by text appearance settings.

subarticles.title: How the text lines up

subarticles.title: Color of typed answers
subarticles.summary: Sets the color of the text a visitor types into this field; the gray placeholder hint has its own separate color. subarticles.title: Variable Binding — every setting
subarticles.summary: Where this screen's answer is stored — the variable, the value each choice maps to, and optional scoring. This guide documents every setting of the Variable Binding block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

subarticles.title: Variable Binding section
subarticles.summary: Variable Binding saves what the visitor chooses or types on this screen as a named value you can reuse later. That saved value is what lets you personalize the funnel: send visitors down different paths based on their answer, segment them in analytics, and pass their details to your paywall and Stripe checkout. Without a binding the answer isn't stored and can't influence anything later, so it appears on every screen that collects an answer.

subarticles.title: Where it appears
subarticles.summary: Covered screen types: ListMultiPick, ListSinglePick, GridMultiPick, GridSinglePick, TextInput, WheelPicker.

subarticles.title: Add an option value
subarticles.summary: Type a value for a new option on this variable and click Add; it joins the options list and the mapping table below. Use a stable, lowercase, underscore-style value such as maintain_weight so routing and analytics stay clean. After adding it, map it to the matching on-screen item below — otherwise a visitor choosing that answer won't store anything.

subarticles.title: Rebuild options from the items
subarticles.summary: A shortcut that rebuilds this variable's options from the screen's current list or grid items so the stored values match what's on screen, handy after you've added or changed items and don't want to re-enter each option by hand. Warning: it replaces the existing options (a confirmation shows old versus new first), so custom options or mappings not present in the items can be lost. Avoid it when the variable is shared with other screens, and most funnels rarely need it once options are set.

subarticles.title: Internal note (optional)
subarticles.summary: An optional internal note explaining what this variable is for. It only shows as a tooltip in the editor when you hover the variable later — visitors never see it and it has no effect on the funnel. A one-line note like "visitor's primary fitness goal" is worth adding so you and teammates remember the variable's purpose when reusing it across screens.

subarticles.title: Name the new variable
subarticles.summary: A readable name for the variable you're creating, like User Goal, that must be unique across the funnel. It becomes the reference you use elsewhere — usually a lowercased, underscored form such as @user_goal in dynamic text and conditions. Pick a clear name that describes the answer (User Goal, Experience Level) rather than the screen, since later references depend on it and you won't want to rename it.

subarticles.title: List the stored answers
subarticles.summary: For Choice and Multiple-choice variables, list the values this variable can store, such as lose_weight, build_muscle, or stay_fit; add, rename, or remove them here. These stored values are separate from the labels visitors see — you connect each one to a visible item in the Value Mapping table below. Keep one option per real answer so your routing and analytics stay clean.

subarticles.title: What kind of value it stores
subarticles.summary: Sets the kind of value this variable holds, which must fit the screen. Use Choice for single-select screens, Multiple choices for multi-select lists or grids where visitors pick several, Number for numeric input like age or weight, and Text for free-form typed answers. The screen only offers compatible types, and the Choice options you can branch and report on are defined below.

subarticles.title: Link a choice to this value
subarticles.summary: Connect this option to the on-screen choice (the list or grid row) that should set it, so when a visitor picks that row the variable stores this value. Each visible choice should map to one option so answers record correctly, and several options can point to the same row if needed. If a choice has no option mapped to it, the editor flags it as unmapped, so fix that before publishing or it won't record an answer.

subarticles.title: The stored value for this option
subarticles.summary: This is the value saved to the variable and used in conditions and analytics, not the text visitors see (that lives on the list or grid item). Keep it stable and lowercase with underscores, like lose_weight. You can rename it, but that changes every place it's referenced, so avoid renaming after the funnel is published and collecting data.

subarticles.title: Points this answer adds
subarticles.summary: The whole number this answer adds to the running total in the target score variable when a visitor selects this option. Give higher-intent answers larger values and weaker ones smaller or zero, for example 'ready to buy' = 10 and 'just browsing' = 1. Keep a consistent scale across all answers so the final total is meaningful for branching or analytics.

subarticles.title: Which score this adds to
subarticles.summary: Choose the number variable this answer adds points to, such as a quiz_score or lead_score total. Only Number-type variables appear here, so if the list is empty, create a number variable first. Use one shared score variable across all the screens you want to total up, with the points set in the score value field.

subarticles.title: Add points based on answers
subarticles.summary: Optional and advanced: have each answer on this screen add points to a number variable, like a quiz or lead-qualification score. You can later branch on the total (high score to a premium paywall) or send it to analytics. Skip this unless you're scoring answers, since most screens don't need it.

subarticles.title: Choose where the answer is saved
subarticles.summary: Pick which variable stores this screen's answer, or create a new one on the spot. Reuse an existing variable when this screen asks about the same thing as another screen (so all answers feed one value), and create a new one for a brand-new question. This is the key step: nothing downstream (branching, analytics, paywall personalization) works until a variable is chosen here.

subarticles.title: Context caption
subarticles.summary: Open the Content section in the screen editor to configure its settings.

subarticles.title: The line under your title
subarticles.summary: The subtitle is the supporting line beneath your title; use it to expand the promise, add proof, or hint at what happens next. Turn it on and keep it to one short sentence; it shows smaller and lighter than the title by default so the headline stays dominant. Like the title, you can personalize it with @ variables. subarticles.title: • Background opacity

subarticles.title: • Background radius
subarticles.summary: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

subarticles.title: • Font family
subarticles.summary: The typeface of the subtitle.

subarticles.title: • Font size
subarticles.summary: Text size of the subtitle in pixels.

subarticles.title: • Font weight
subarticles.summary: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

subarticles.title: • Line height
subarticles.summary: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

subarticles.title: • Strikethrough color
subarticles.summary: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

subarticles.title: • Text align
subarticles.summary: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

subarticles.title: • Text background color
subarticles.summary: An optional fill drawn behind the subtitle text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

subarticles.title: • Text color
subarticles.summary: The color of the subtitle text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

subarticles.title: The line under your title
subarticles.summary: The line under your title

subarticles.title: Space around the subtitle
subarticles.summary: Adds empty space on each side of the subtitle, controlling the gap above it (to the title) and below it (to what follows). Leave it at the theme default unless the subtitle feels crowded. Increase the top value to separate it from the title, or reduce spacing to tighten the whole headline group.

subarticles.title: Space around the subtitle

subarticles.title: Write the subtitle text
subarticles.summary: Type the supporting line that sits under your title here, one short sentence that reinforces the offer or tells the visitor what comes next. If your funnel is multilingual, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

Type @ to drop in an earlier answer (for example @user_goal) so it feels personal, and style it under the gear icon below.

subarticles.title: Title look and emphasis

subarticles.title: Write the headline text
subarticles.summary: Write the headline text

subarticles.title: The featured image up top
subarticles.summary: The hero is the large featured image at the top of a headline or wheel-picker screen, the picture that sells the screen at a glance. Turn it on, then upload a file or paste an image URL. Pick a high-quality, on-message visual (product, result, or lifestyle shot); on a paid landing page it is often the first thing a visitor sees. Sizing and position are set just below.

subarticles.title: How rounded the image is
subarticles.summary: Rounds all four corners of the hero image; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer and more rounded. The default is 0. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, friendly look; match it to the rounding used elsewhere in your funnel, like buttons and cards, so the page feels consistent.

subarticles.title: How rounded the image is
subarticles.summary: How rounded the image is

subarticles.title: Fixed image height
subarticles.summary: Optionally pin the hero image to a set height with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty to let the image keep its natural proportions from the width — best for most screens. Use a fixed height when you want a consistent banner size; to size by screen proportion instead, use 'Image height relative to container' below, which takes priority over this value.

subarticles.title: Fixed image height
subarticles.summary: Fixed image height

subarticles.title: Size the image by screen
subarticles.summary: Sizes the hero image as a percentage of the screen height (0 to 100%), so it scales with the device, the more responsive way to size a hero. If set, it overrides any fixed height above. A common starting point is 30 to 50% for a prominent banner that still leaves room for your title and button below; leave it empty to size by proportions instead.

subarticles.title: Size the image by screen
subarticles.summary: Size the image by screen

subarticles.title: Fixed image width
subarticles.summary: Optionally pin the hero image to a set width with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty in most cases — the image then sizes to the screen and stays responsive across devices, which almost always looks best on a landing page. Set a fixed width only when you need the image smaller than full-width or aligned to a specific size.

subarticles.title: Fixed image width
subarticles.summary: Fixed image width

subarticles.title: How the image fills its box
subarticles.summary: Sets how your image fits its box: Aspect Fit shows the whole image with no cropping (you may see empty bars at the sides), Aspect Fill crops the edges so it fully covers the box, Scale to Fill stretches it (can look distorted, avoid for photos), and Tile repeats it as a pattern. Default is Aspect Fit, which never distorts; switch to Aspect Fill when you want it edge-to-edge and don't mind some cropping.

subarticles.title: How the image fills its box
subarticles.summary: How the image fills its box

subarticles.title: The featured image up top
subarticles.summary: The featured image up top

subarticles.title: Space around the image
subarticles.summary: Adds empty space on each side of the hero image (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or crammed next to the title. Leave it at the theme default in most cases. Increase a side when the image feels too tight against nearby content, or reduce it for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge look.

subarticles.title: Space around the image
subarticles.summary: Space around the image

subarticles.title: The hero image itself
subarticles.summary: Pick the actual hero image: upload a file from your computer or paste a direct image URL, then check the preview thumbnail. Use a high-resolution JPG or PNG so it stays crisp on large screens — uploads are optimized automatically for fast loading. To change it later, just upload or paste a new source here.

subarticles.title: Where the image sits

The preview updates instantly, so try a couple and keep whichever reads clearest.

subarticles.title: Hero image
subarticles.summary: The Hero image is the lead visual above the text. This guide documents every Hero image setting — the image source, how it is sized, rounded and spaced, and how the image and text are arranged.

subarticles.title: The featured image up top
subarticles.summary: The hero is the large featured image at the top of a headline or wheel-picker screen, the picture that sells the screen at a glance. Turn it on, then upload a file or paste an image URL. Pick a high-quality, on-message visual (product, result, or lifestyle shot); on a paid landing page it is often the first thing a visitor sees. Sizing and position are set just below.

subarticles.title: How rounded the image is
subarticles.summary: Rounds all four corners of the hero image; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer and more rounded. The default is 0. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, friendly look; match it to the rounding used elsewhere in your funnel, like buttons and cards, so the page feels consistent.

subarticles.title: Fixed image height
subarticles.summary: Optionally pin the hero image to a set height with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty to let the image keep its natural proportions from the width — best for most screens. Use a fixed height when you want a consistent banner size; to size by screen proportion instead, use 'Image height relative to container' below, which takes priority over this value.

subarticles.title: Size the image by screen
subarticles.summary: Sizes the hero image as a percentage of the screen height (0 to 100%), so it scales with the device, the more responsive way to size a hero. If set, it overrides any fixed height above. A common starting point is 30 to 50% for a prominent banner that still leaves room for your title and button below; leave it empty to size by proportions instead.

subarticles.title: Fixed image width
subarticles.summary: Optionally pin the hero image to a set width with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty in most cases — the image then sizes to the screen and stays responsive across devices, which almost always looks best on a landing page. Set a fixed width only when you need the image smaller than full-width or aligned to a specific size.

subarticles.title: How the image fills its box
subarticles.summary: Sets how your image fits its box: Aspect Fit shows the whole image with no cropping (you may see empty bars at the sides), Aspect Fill crops the edges so it fully covers the box, Scale to Fill stretches it (can look distorted, avoid for photos), and Tile repeats it as a pattern. Default is Aspect Fit, which never distorts; switch to Aspect Fill when you want it edge-to-edge and don't mind some cropping.

subarticles.summary: Appearance of the selection checkbox — shape (square or circle), checked color, unchecked color, and padding. subarticles.title: Grid cell proportions
subarticles.summary: Sets each grid cell's height as a percentage of its width: 100 is square, above 100 makes taller cells, below 100 makes wider, shorter cells. Pick taller cells for image-led options and square for balanced icon-and-text choices. Only appears on two-column grids — try 100 first, then adjust to fit your content.

subarticles.title: Grid cell proportions
subarticles.summary: Grid cell proportions

subarticles.title: Checkbox placement in grid cells
subarticles.summary: On grid cells, show or hide the selection checkbox and place it in a corner (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right) with an optional offset. Keep it visible on multi-select grids so visitors can see what they've picked; top-right is a common, unobtrusive spot. Only appears on grid layouts.

subarticles.summary: Gap between the checkbox and the cell edges (top, right, bottom, left).

subarticles.title: • Position
subarticles.summary: Which corner of the cell the checkbox sits in (top-start, top-end, bottom-start, bottom-end).

subarticles.title: • Show checkbox

subarticles.title: Checkbox look
subarticles.summary: Appearance of the selection checkbox — shape (square or circle), checked color, unchecked color, and padding. Only appears when the layout includes a checkbox or on grids.

subarticles.summary: Space around the selection marker.

subarticles.summary: Color of the marker when the option is selected.

subarticles.title: • Shape
subarticles.summary: The selection-marker shape (square or circle).

subarticles.title: • Unchecked color
subarticles.summary: Color of the marker when the option is not selected.

subarticles.title: Image area in each card
subarticles.summary: On grid cards that show an image, this sets the image region as a whole: where it sits in the card, how tall it is (a fixed height or sized to fit its content), and the spacing around it. By default it fits the content, but setting one fixed height keeps every card's image lined up at the same level, which looks more polished and trustworthy on an ad landing page. This shapes the image's container only; the image's own size and corners are set separately in the item image styles.

subarticles.summary: Image area in each card

subarticles.title: • Content align
subarticles.summary: Horizontal alignment of the image inside the region.

subarticles.title: • Height mode
subarticles.summary: How the image region is sized: a fixed pixel height, a percent of the cell, or auto.

subarticles.title: • Height value
subarticles.summary: The height number used by the chosen mode (px or %).

subarticles.title: • Region padding
subarticles.summary: Empty space inside the image region around the image (top, right, bottom, left).

subarticles.title: • Vertical align
subarticles.summary: Where the image sits within its region — top, center, or bottom.

subarticles.title: Item image look
subarticles.summary: Size and look of each item's image — width, height, corner radius, padding, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole image with possible empty space; fill crops to cover the box). Keep a consistent size and small radius so cards look uniform; choose fill for photos and fit for logos or icons you don't want cropped. Only appears when the layout includes an image.

subarticles.title: Item image look
subarticles.summary: Item image look

subarticles.title: • Corner radius
subarticles.summary: How rounded the image corners are.

subarticles.title: • Image height
subarticles.summary: Height (px) of the option's image or icon.

subarticles.title: • Image padding
subarticles.summary: Space around the image inside the option.

subarticles.title: • Image width
subarticles.summary: Width (px) of the option's image or icon.

subarticles.title: • Scale mode
subarticles.summary: How the image fills its box (fit, fill, or stretch).

subarticles.title: Shuffle item order
subarticles.summary: When enabled, randomizes the order items appear to users on each view. Useful for A/B testing, survey randomization, and reducing position bias in multi-select scenarios.

subarticles.title: Shuffle item order
subarticles.summary: Shuffle item order

subarticles.title: What each choice shows
subarticles.summary: Pick which parts each choice displays — title only, image plus title, checkbox with title and subtitle, and so on; available combos depend on your selection mode and layout. Adding an element reveals its style controls and means you must supply that content (image or subtitle) on every item. Default to title (plus a checkbox for multi-select) and add an image only when it aids the choice.

subarticles.title: What each choice shows
subarticles.summary: What each choice shows

subarticles.title: Padding inside each item
subarticles.summary: The space between each item's edge and its content (title, image, checkbox), set per side — top, end, bottom, start. More padding makes items feel roomy and easier to tap; too little looks cramped. Around 12–16px on all sides reads well on mobile, and the setting applies to every item.

subarticles.title: Padding inside each item
subarticles.summary: Padding inside each item

subarticles.title: Gap between choices
subarticles.summary: The spacing between adjacent choices — a vertical gap in lists, the gap between cells in grids. Around 8–12px keeps items clearly separate and easy to tap without wasting space. Increase it for a more airy feel, or decrease it to fit more options above the fold.

subarticles.title: Gap between choices
subarticles.summary: Gap between choices

subarticles.title: Margin around the whole list
subarticles.summary: The outer space between the screen edges and the first and last items, set per side (top, end, bottom, start). Use it to keep the list off the screen edges and aligned with your other sections. This is the outside spacing — for the gap inside each item use Padding inside each item instead.

subarticles.title: Margin around the whole list
subarticles.summary: Margin around the whole list

subarticles.title: Cap on multi-select picks
subarticles.summary: Limits how many items a visitor can choose on a multi-select screen. Set a small cap (e.g. 3) to keep answers focused and the next step manageable; leave it unlimited to let them pick freely. This control only appears on multi-select screens and is ignored everywhere else.

subarticles.title: Cap on multi-select picks
subarticles.summary: Cap on multi-select picks

subarticles.summary: How a choice looks once tapped — background, border, corner radius, and optional gradient. Your theme's accent color is a reliable choice.

subarticles.summary: Corner rounding for the selected option; usually matches the unselected state.

subarticles.summary: Typography for the item subtitle — size, weight, color, alignment, line height, optional background, and padding, applied to all items as a shared template. subarticles.title: The line under your title
subarticles.summary: The subtitle is the supporting line beneath your title; use it to expand the promise, add proof, or hint at what happens next. Turn it on and keep it to one short sentence; it shows smaller and lighter than the title by default so the headline stays dominant. Like the title, you can personalize it with @ variables. Skip it on screens where the title already says everything.

subarticles.title: Subtitle look and emphasis
subarticles.summary: Change how the subtitle looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional background — styled separately from the title so you can tune each one. By default it inherits your theme (usually smaller and lighter than the title), which works for most funnels. Override only when a specific screen needs different emphasis.

subarticles.title: Subtitle look and emphasis
subarticles.summary: Subtitle look and emphasis

subarticles.title: • Background opacity
subarticles.summary: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

subarticles.title: • Background radius
subarticles.summary: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

subarticles.title: • Font family
subarticles.summary: The typeface of the subtitle.

subarticles.title: • Font size
subarticles.summary: Text size of the subtitle in pixels.

subarticles.title: • Font weight
subarticles.summary: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

subarticles.title: • Line height
subarticles.summary: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

subarticles.title: • Strikethrough color
subarticles.summary: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

subarticles.title: • Text align
subarticles.summary: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

subarticles.title: • Text background color
subarticles.summary: An optional fill drawn behind the subtitle text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

subarticles.title: • Text color
subarticles.summary: The color of the subtitle text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

subarticles.title: The line under your title
subarticles.summary: The line under your title

subarticles.title: Space around the subtitle
subarticles.summary: Adds empty space on each side of the subtitle, controlling the gap above it (to the title) and below it (to what follows). Leave it at the theme default unless the subtitle feels crowded. Increase the top value to separate it from the title, or reduce spacing to tighten the whole headline group.

subarticles.title: Space around the subtitle
subarticles.summary: Space around the subtitle

subarticles.title: Write the subtitle text
subarticles.summary: Type the supporting line that sits under your title here, one short sentence that reinforces the offer or tells the visitor what comes next. The same shortcuts work as in the title: type @ to insert an earlier answer, @link to add a clickable link, or @countdown for urgency. If your funnel is multilingual, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

subarticles.title: Write the subtitle text
subarticles.summary: Write the subtitle text

subarticles.title: Your main headline
subarticles.summary: The title is the biggest, first thing a visitor reads, so it carries most of the weight on whether they keep going. Turn it on, then write one short benefit-led line, like an ad headline rather than a sentence. Type @ to drop in an earlier answer (for example @user_goal) so it feels personal, and style it under the gear icon below.

subarticles.title: Title look and emphasis
subarticles.summary: Override how the headline looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional highlight behind the text. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent, so most funnels never need to touch this. Override only when one screen needs extra punch, like a bigger color headline on your hero.

subarticles.title: Title look and emphasis
subarticles.summary: Title look and emphasis

subarticles.title: • Background opacity
subarticles.summary: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

subarticles.title: • Background radius

subarticles.summary: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

subarticles.title: • Strikethrough color

subarticles.title: • Text align

subarticles.summary: An optional fill drawn behind the title text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

subarticles.summary: Your main headline

subarticles.title: Space around the title
subarticles.summary: Adds empty space on each side of the title (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't cramped against the screen edges or the text below. Leave it at the theme default unless the title feels too tight or too far from the next element. Increase a side to give it room, or decrease to pull elements closer together.

subarticles.title: Space around the title
subarticles.summary: Space around the title

subarticles.title: Write the headline text
subarticles.summary: This is where you type the actual headline; keep it short and benefit-driven. Type @ to pull in a visitor's earlier answer (such as @user_goal) for personalization, add a link inside the text with @link, or insert a countdown with @countdown to create urgency on offer screens. If your funnel runs in more than one language, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

subarticles.title: Write the headline text
subarticles.summary: Write the headline text

subarticles.title: The featured image up top
subarticles.summary: The hero is the large featured image at the top of a headline or wheel-picker screen, the picture that sells the screen at a glance. Turn it on, then upload a file or paste an image URL. Pick a high-quality, on-message visual (product, result, or lifestyle shot); on a paid landing page it is often the first thing a visitor sees. Sizing and position are set just below.

subarticles.title: How rounded the image is
subarticles.summary: Rounds all four corners of the hero image; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer and more rounded. The default is 0. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, friendly look; match it to the rounding used elsewhere in your funnel, like buttons and cards, so the page feels consistent.

subarticles.title: How rounded the image is
subarticles.summary: How rounded the image is

subarticles.title: Fixed image height
subarticles.summary: Optionally pin the hero image to a set height with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty to let the image keep its natural proportions from the width — best for most screens. Use a fixed height when you want a consistent banner size; to size by screen proportion instead, use 'Image height relative to container' below, which takes priority over this value.

subarticles.title: Fixed image height
subarticles.summary: Fixed image height

subarticles.title: Size the image by screen
subarticles.summary: Sizes the hero image as a percentage of the screen height (0 to 100%), so it scales with the device, the more responsive way to size a hero. If set, it overrides any fixed height above. A common starting point is 30 to 50% for a prominent banner that still leaves room for your title and button below; leave it empty to size by proportions instead.

subarticles.title: Size the image by screen
subarticles.summary: Size the image by screen

subarticles.title: Fixed image width
subarticles.summary: Optionally pin the hero image to a set width with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty in most cases — the image then sizes to the screen and stays responsive across devices, which almost always looks best on a landing page. Set a fixed width only when you need the image smaller than full-width or aligned to a specific size.

subarticles.title: Fixed image width
subarticles.summary: Fixed image width

subarticles.title: How the image fills its box
subarticles.summary: Sets how your image fits its box: Aspect Fit shows the whole image with no cropping (you may see empty bars at the sides), Aspect Fill crops the edges so it fully covers the box, Scale to Fill stretches it (can look distorted, avoid for photos), and Tile repeats it as a pattern. Default is Aspect Fit, which never distorts; switch to Aspect Fill when you want it edge-to-edge and don't mind some cropping.

subarticles.title: How the image fills its box
subarticles.summary: How the image fills its box

subarticles.title: The featured image up top
subarticles.summary: The featured image up top

subarticles.title: Space around the image
subarticles.summary: Adds empty space on each side of the hero image (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or crammed next to the title. Leave it at the theme default in most cases. Increase a side when the image feels too tight against nearby content, or reduce it for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge look.

subarticles.title: Space around the image
subarticles.summary: Space around the image

subarticles.title: The hero image itself
subarticles.summary: Pick the actual hero image: upload a file from your computer or paste a direct image URL, then check the preview thumbnail. Use a high-resolution JPG or PNG so it stays crisp on large screens — uploads are optimized automatically for fast loading. To change it later, just upload or paste a new source here.

subarticles.title: The hero image itself
subarticles.summary: The hero image itself

subarticles.title: Where the image sits
subarticles.summary: On headline screens, this sets where the hero image sits relative to your title and subtitle — above the text, below it, or beside it. Lead with your strongest element: image-on-top when the visual is the hook, text-on-top when the headline does the selling. The preview updates instantly, so try a couple and keep whichever reads clearest.

articles.title: Analytics setup
articles.oneLineSummary: Explains the Analytics setup section in Integrations and why tracking should be configured before sending traffic. It covers choosing the correct analytics destination, verifying that visits, screen events, checkout transitions, and purchase signals arrive, and optionally enabling GDPR consent controls before publishing a funnel.

subarticles.title: Enable GDPR consent management (optional)
subarticles.summary: Toggle consent management to show a consent banner in regulated regions. You set the default consent state, banner text, and privacy policy URL, and consent decisions gate which events are collected.

subarticles.title: Choose the provider, then verify
subarticles.summary: Pick the analytics platform that matches your reporting workflow, then publish a test funnel and confirm events arrive in that provider dashboard within seconds.

subarticles.title: Track the funnel before scaling
subarticles.summary: Set up and verify analytics before publishing to traffic. Events are measured from the first visitor, so a destination added later cannot capture earlier sessions.

articles.title: Custom Domain setup
articles.oneLineSummary: Explains the Custom Domain setup flow for replacing a generic Segmently link with a branded domain. It covers the order of entering the domain, adding DNS records at the customer's domain provider, verifying the domain in Segmently, and publishing only after the domain is ready.

subarticles.title: Why a custom domain matters
subarticles.summary: A custom domain (for example funnel.example.com) swaps the generic Segmently link for your own brand. A branded link looks more trustworthy in ads and emails, so more people click and fewer drop off before reaching your funnel. It's optional — publishing still works fine on the default Segmently domain if you skip it.

subarticles.title: Recommended order of steps
subarticles.summary: Work through it in this order: (1) enter your domain, (2) add the DNS records Segmently shows you at your domain provider, (3) click Verify and wait for the 'Verified' status, then (4) select that verified domain when you publish a Web Placement. Verification has to succeed before the domain can serve your live funnel, so don't publish against it until the status is green.

articles.title: Launch a paid funnel you can run ads against: the complete order of steps
articles.oneLineSummary: Gives the recommended end-to-end order for launching a paid funnel that can receive ad traffic. It covers setup dependencies such as Stripe, paywall products, analytics, onboarding screens, web placement or URL routing, publish verification, and how to avoid skipping payment or tracking prerequisites.

articles.title: Payment methods on your paywall: embedded vs redirect, cards & wallets
articles.oneLineSummary: Explains payment method behavior on Segmently paywalls, including embedded checkout versus redirect-style checkout, card payments, Apple Pay or wallet availability, Stripe configuration dependencies, and how payment method choices relate to the paywall purchase experience.

articles.title: Every event Segmently sends to TikTok (Pixel + Events API)
articles.oneLineSummary: Lists the TikTok Pixel and Events API events that Segmently can send from a funnel, including visitor activity, onboarding interactions, product catalog selection, checkout, and purchase-related signals. Use this when customers ask what TikTok events are emitted or how TikTok tracking maps to funnel behavior.

articles.title: Set up the TikTok Pixel and Events API
articles.oneLineSummary: Shows how to connect TikTok analytics to Segmently by configuring the TikTok Pixel and Events API credentials, then verifying that funnel events can be sent. Use this for setup questions about TikTok Pixel, Events API tokens, provider configuration, and analytics readiness.
